drivingQuestion: Why, for Abba Shaul, does a court-appointed steward swear?
outcomeNote: the court-appointed steward's benefit is his reputation

segments.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: חִילּוּף הַדְּבָרִים: מַאי טַעְמָא מִינּוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין – יִשָּׁבַע? בְּהַהִיא הֲנָאָה דְּקָא נָפֵיק עֲלֵיהּ קָלָא דְּאִינִישׁ מְהֵימְנָא הוּא – דְּהָא סָמֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ בֵּי דִינָא – מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעָה לָא אָתֵי לְאִמְּנוֹעֵי.
segments.en: The mishna then teaches: «Abba Shaul says: The matters are reversed;» it is not a steward appointed by the orphans’ father but a steward appointed by the court who takes an oath. The Gemara clarifies Abba Shaul’s opinion: «What is the reason» that if «the court appointed» the steward, «he takes an oath? Since» he derives «a certain benefit» from his appointment, «that publicity is generated about him that he is a trustworthy man, as» is demonstrated by the fact that «the court relies upon him» and appoints him to a position of responsibility, «he will not come to avoid» becoming a steward merely «because of an oath» that the court will impose upon him.
